abstract: Objectives Alcohol dependence accounts for a large proportion of the global burden of disease and disability. This study aims to investigate the candidate genes and chemicals associated with alcohol dependence. Methods Using data from published alcohol dependence genome-wide association studies, we first conducted a proteome-wide association study of alcohol dependence by integrating alcohol dependence genome-wide association studies with 2 human brain reference proteomes of dorsolateral prefrontal cortex from the Religious Order Study and Rush Memory and Aging Project and the Banner Sun Health Research Institute. Then, based on the identified genes in proteome-wide association study, we conducted functional enrichment analysis and chemical-related functional enrichment analysis to detect the related Gene Ontology terms and chemicals. Results Proteome-wide association study identified several potential candidate genes for alcohol dependence, such as GOT2 ( P = 7.59 × 10 −6 ) and C3orf33 ( P = 5.00 × 10 −3 ). Furthermore, functional enrichment analysis identified multiple candidate Gene Ontology terms associated with alcohol dependence, such as glyoxylate metabolic process (adjusted P = 2.99 × 10 −6 ) and oxoglutarate metabolic process (adjusted P = 9.95 × 10 −6 ). Chemical-related functional enrichment analysis detected several alcohol dependence–related candidate chemicals, such as pitavastatin ( P = 2.00 × 10 −4 ), cannabinoids ( P = 4.00 × 10 −4 ), 11-nor-Δ(9)-tetrahydrocannabinol-9-carboxylic acid ( P = 4.00 × 10 −4 ), and gabapentin ( P = 2.00 × 10 −3 ). Conclusions Our study reports multiple candidate genes and chemicals associated with alcohol dependence, providing novel clues for understanding the biological mechanism of alcohol dependence.
methods:
METHODS
GWAS Summary Data of Alcohol Dependence
The GWAS summary data of alcohol dependence were derived from a previous study.
20
We selected GWAS summary data in the meta-analysis of unrelated European samples for further analyses, and all of the patients in this analysis were restricted to European Whites, including 10,206 cases and 24,480 controls. All of the genotypes data were saved on a secure server, and quality control (QC) and imputation were performed using RICOPILI pipeline (
https://github.com/Nealelab/ricopili
) and PICOPILI pipeline (
https://github.com/Nealelab/picopili
). IMPUTE2 and SHAPEIT were used for cohort imputation. We selected GWAS summary data in the meta-analysis of unrelated European samples for further analyses. A detailed description of the sample characteristics, experimental design, QC, imputation, and statistical analysis can be found in the published study.
20
Human Brain Proteome Reference Weight
Human brain proteomes were generated from 2 projects. First, the dPFC of 400 participants of European descent was obtained from the Religious Order Study and Rush Memory and Aging Project (ROS/MAP).
21
All of the enrolled participants signed an informed consent, and the study was approved by the Institutional Review Board of Rush University Medical Center. Then, the dPFC of 152 participants of European descent recruited by Banner Sun Health Research Institute was used to improve the credibility of our research,
22
and all of the subjects signed an informed consent form. After QC and regressing out the effects of clinical characteristics and technical factors, we estimated the effects of genetic variants on protein abundance, which we designated as protein weights. Liquid chromatography–tandem mass spectrometry and isobaric tandem mass tag were used for proteomics analysis. For QC of the proteome, the proteins with missing values in more than 50% were eliminated. Using sample-specific total protein abundance, each protein abundance was scaled and then log2-transformed to remove the effects of protein loading differences. Outliers were identified and removed using iterative principal component analysis, that is, samples with 4 or more SDs from the mean on the first or second principal component are considered outliers.
23
Before estimating the protein weights, the effects of proteomic sequencing batch, sex, age, final clinical diagnosis of cognitive status, and postmortem interval from the confirmation proteomic profiles were removed using regression analysis.
Proteome-wide Association Studies
We integrated reference human brain proteomes with the abovementioned latest alcohol dependence GWAS results to perform a PWAS using the FUSION pipeline (
http://gusevlab.org/projects/fusion/
). Whole-brain proteomic analysis of dPFC was performed to estimate protein abundance for each participant. First, the protein weights of 2 human brain proteomes, ROS/MAP and Banner, were estimated in the FUSION pipeline (ROS/MAP and Banner analysis processes were identical). Second, alcohol dependence genetic effects (GWAS
z
score) were calculated and combined with precomputed brain proteome reference weights (
z
score × proteome weight) to assess the impact of significant SNPs on protein abundance in GWAS. Finally, FUSION was used to determine whether potential gene protein abundances are correlated to alcohol dependence. The analysis was conducted using the default FUSION parameters and settings (the major operating parameters are as follows: –sumstats, –weights, –weights_dir, –chr, –ref_ld_chr, –out, –perm, and –GWASN; additional information on the pipeline can be found in the FUSION tutorial guideline). To control the potential impact of multiple test issues, we performed 5000 permutation tests in FUSION and generated a permutation-based
P
value (named PERM.ANL).
Functional Enrichment Analysis of PWAS Identified Genes
In this study, we used the GENE2FUNC function of the FUMA online tool (
https://fuma.ctglab.nl/
) for functional enrichment analysis of genes identified by PWAS.
24
The major function of FUMA includes SNP2GENE and GENE2FUNC. In this study, GENE3FUNC was used to perform the tissue specificity analysis. GENE2FUNC offers several outputs, including enrichment analysis of differentially expressed genes (DEGs), overrepresentation of gene sets, links to external biological of input genes, and a heat map of gene expression.
24
For GENE2FUNC, genes are tested against those DEG sets by a hypergeometric test to assess whether prioritized genes (genes of interest) are overrepresented in the DEG set for a particular tissue type.
24
To avoid the implementation of optimal normalization of raw data, mRNA expression data sets applied in GENE2FUNC have been generated through different independent studies based-analysis pipelines.
25
Biological functions of identified proteins were annotated as 3 functional categories: biological process, cellular component, and in the Gene Ontology (GO) database. Gene Ontology characterizes the relationships among genes by particularly annotating and categorizing molecular functions of gene products and associated biological process.
26
A
P
value threshold of <0.05 was considered to be significant.
Chemical-Gene Expression Annotation Dataset
We evaluated relationships among gene expressions and chemicals from CTD (
http://ctdbase.org/downloads/
), a database containing related toxicological information for genes, chemicals, diseases and phenotypes. Currently, CTD provides more than 1,363,085 interactions between 11,808 chemicals and 40,862 genes in 562 organisms.
27
There are different sets of sample data in CTD, such as chemical-disease associations, chemical element-phenotype associations, chemical-gene interactions, and gene-disease associations,
28
in which chemical-gene interaction annotation information was used. Approximately 11,190 chemical-related gene sets were generated and analyzed in this study.
Chemical-related Functional Enrichment Analysis
Enrichment analysis was conducted to explore the association between chemicals and alcohol dependence via a weighted Kolmogorov-Smirnov running-sun statistic, using chemical PWAS
Z
statistics and related gene sets generated by CTD.
29
,
30
Approximately 5000 permutations were performed to determine the empirical distributions of GSEA statistics for each chemical. One of the confounding factors of GSEA performance is the variable size of the gene sets; thus, we eliminated gene sets that included <5 and ≥200 genes. All of the analyses were performed using R 4.1.0 software. A
P
value of <0.05 was accepted as the threshold of statistical significance.

body:
Alcohol overuse includes alcohol dependence and a harmful pattern of alcohol use that result in severe health problems and have also become a social burden. Based on
Diagnostic and Statistical Manual of Mental Disorders
criteria, individuals with alcohol dependence are usually undergo preoccupied with alcohol, lose control with alcohol intake, have frequent episodes of intoxication, and develop a negative emotional state without alcohol.
1
Alcohol consumption has caused about 7% of total number of deaths reported and roughly 50% of the total number of disability-adjusted life years.
2
It has also been shown that alcohol consumption caused 2.07 million deaths in males and 0.374 million deaths in females in 2019.
3
Excess alcohol consumption impairs the functions of many organs and systems, thereby affecting human health. Compared with individuals with low alcohol consumption, individuals with alcohol use disorder (AUD) are more susceptible to cardiovascular disease, heart failure, and premature death.
4
There is growing evidence that alcohol dependence is a complex disorder that results from the combination of genetic and environmental factors. The factors affecting the development of alcohol dependence include culture, religion, family environment, and childhood adversity.
5
However, genetic factors seem to make a larger contribution to alcohol dependence. Alcohol dependence has been reported to be 50% heritable,
6
and genetic liability to alcoholism may be greater in males than females. Furthermore, animal experiments have indicated that genetic manipulation is associated with decreased alcohol consumption.
7
Aldehyde dehydrogenase 2 (
ALDH2
) is a well-recognized gene that is related to alcohol consumption; it has been regarded as a risk factor for progression to alcohol-related medical problems, whereas it is considered as a protective factor against progression to heavy drinking.
5
Alcohol misuse has also been associated with brain areas, such as prefrontal regions, white matter, and dorsolateral prefrontal cortex (dPFC).
8
,
9
Addiction (including alcoholism) has been reported to be associated with dPFC dysfunction, whose stimulation attenuates drug craving,
8
and plays an important role in motivated behaviors. Regular alcohol misuse leads to marked dPFC atrophy. It has been suggested that alcohol dependence is related to the decrease or loss of neurons in the dPFC.
10
Furthermore, alcoholism leads to the decreased expression of dPFC messenger RNA (mRNA) of specific genes. There is a borderline significance in κ-opioid receptor mRNA and prodynorphin in the dPFC and orbitofrontal cortex of alcoholics.
11
In addition, environmental factors, such as chemicals exposure, have been suggested to be related to brain development and dysfunction, despite the presence of manganese in the air, food, and water at low levels; its concentrations are associated to intellectual function and hyperactivity among school-age children.
12
,
13
Observational and experimental studies have shown that prenatal phthalate exposure is associated with both behavioral abnormalities and neurodevelopmental deficits, leading to conduct disorder and shortened attention span in offspring.
14
Chemicals can also affect the development of human complex disorders through altered methylation, mutagenesis, and physical interactions.
15
Based on this evidence, we hypothesize that chemicals are closely related to brain development.
Comparative Toxicogenomics Database (CTD) is a robust, publicly available database, which provides information about interactions of chemical-gene/protein, relationships between chemical-disease and gene disease. Davis et al
15
showed that, if chemical A is associated with gene B, and gene B is related to disease C, then it may be assumed that chemical A is related to disease C, and there is correlative evidence to support this approach, such as that for arsenic. However, the biological mechanism of chemicals implicated in the development of alcohol dependence remains largely unknown.
Genome-wide association study (GWAS) is used to identify genetic markers associated with phenotypic variations. Although GWAS detects a majority of significant genetic variants that are located in noncoding regions, the impact of noncoding regions on the development of target diseases is difficult to interpret.
16
Proteome-wide association study (PWAS) is a new method for detecting gene-phenotype associations mediated by protein function alterations. Based on the premise that causal variants in coding regions affect phenotypes by altering the biochemical functions of the gene protein products, PWAS can identify loci that confer alcohol dependence risk through their effects on brain protein abundance, thereby providing new insights into the pathogenesis of complex diseases. Proteome-wide association study has been widely applied to research studies on mental health. For instance, 19 genes associated with depression and several genes for cognitive trajectory were all detected by PWAS.
17
,
18
These findings indicate novel potential pathogenic mechanisms and new therapeutic targets for disease.
Gene set enrichment analysis (GSEA) has become a standard procedure to identify groups of genes that share regulation, chromosomal location, and common biological function. Gene set enrichment analysis mainly focuses on determining the association between patterns of gene expression and phenotypic class distinction, and providing additional information that is easily ignored by traditional methods.
19
In the study, based on previous GWAS summary data, we conducted PWAS and GSEA to explore potential pathogenic brain proteins and chemicals related to alcohol dependence.

DISCUSSION
Although the environment plays an important role in alcohol dependence, this disorder has been proven to be 50% heritable.
6
Identifying related genes that affect risk of alcohol dependence may help elucidate the underlying mechanism of alcohol dependence and further improve its prevention, diagnosis, and treatment.
In this study, PWAS identified a novel candidate gene
GOT2
associated with alcohol dependence.
GOT2
is a mitochondrial enzyme that plays a role in amino acid metabolism and the urea and tricarboxylic acid cycles (TCAs),
31
and it is involved in generating aspartate for nucleotide biosynthesis and malate-aspartate shuttle. Recently published research showed that
GOT2
is related to alcohol consumption, in Asians.
32
Our study further indicated that
GOT2
is associated with alcohol consumption in a European population. More research is needed to explore how it affects the biological mechanism of alcohol dependence.
The neuroimmune system may contribute to alcohol dependence, particularly innate immune responses in the central and peripheral nervous systems. Glia cells are known to secrete and express neuroimmune molecules. There is a consensus that neuroimmune molecules play a major role in the brain and regulate alcohol behaviors via modulation of the neuronal function.
33
Some of the first microarray analyses of human postmortem brain tissue from alcoholics identified upregulated immune-related genes.
34
CD200
is a novel neuroimmune regulatory proteins that encodes a type I membrane glycoprotein and is expressed by various cell types.
CD200-
expressing B cells belong to Breg family, which produces interleukin (IL)-10. Interleukin 10 signaling plays important regulatory roles in escalating alcohol intake. Previous studies have observed reduced interleukin-10-R (IL10-R) levels in the amygdala and cortex in humans with AUD.
35
In addition, it has been reported that IL-10 could decrease negative emotional states, which are responsible for the increase in alcohol intake during the development of dependence.
36
Reports have shown that there is a significant difference between
CD200
serum levels in alcohol dependence patients, during alcohol withdrawal and 1 month of abstinence,
37
which provides evidence for the indispensable role of neuroimmune regulatory proteins in neuroadaptation during alcohol consumption.
More importantly, we obtained 236 significant candidate chemicals involved in alcohol dependence. Cannabis has a long history of application and is the most abused substance in the world. Cannabinoids are the active ingredients of marijuana and comprise naturally occurring oxygen-containing aromatic hydrocarbon compounds. There are numerous synthetic cannabinoids, which increases the likelihood of developing addiction. The role of different Δ9-tetrahydrocannabinols (THCs) is not fully understood, although most research articles have shown that THC is harmful to human health. Some studies have shown that regional brain volumes, brain stem, white matter integrity along the left temporal lobe, and bilateral thalamus are reduced among users of cannabinoids compared with subjects who never used cannabinoids.
38
Furthermore, brain volumetric studies indicated a decrease of gray matter volume among users of substance dependence.
39
Alcohol dependence is one of the substance dependences; consequently, this evidence shows that people who with cannabinoids are more likely to be susceptible to problematic alcohol use. Cannabinoids interact with the endocannabinoid system,
38
which regulates numerous biological processes, including development, learning, and memory; response to natural rewards energy metabolism; and emotional processing.
38
Endocannabinoid system mainly exists in the peripheral nervous system and human brain, which have been studied as a potential target in treating AUD, especially for CBD. Treatment with CBD reduces inflammation with alcohol intake, which also could reduce alcohol-related brain damage. Some studies have shown that CBD ameliorates central and peripheral inflammation, which is due to improvement of AUD sequelae. Cannabinoid not only decreases craving and consumption of alcohol in animals but also is associated with changes in the expression of key AUD genes,
40
indicating both positive and negative effects of different cannabinoids on human health.
Gabapentin is a structural analog of gamma-aminobutyric acid (GABA), which was approved for the treatment epileptic seizures and neuropathic pain by the Food and Drug Administration. Gabapentin has unique pharmacologic characteristics and can indirectly affect GABA via a specific α-2d subunit. It has been reported to be effective in preventing heavy drinking relapse
41
; there was less alcohol consumption relapse and more total abstinence after the administration of gabapentin, which has low abuse potential and rarely produces alcohol withdrawal symptoms.
42
Furieri and Nakamura-Palacios
43
also supported the efficiency of gabapentin to treat alcohol dependence and withdrawal.
Lysophosphatidic acid has wide biological activities, including adequate development of organisms and regulation of protein synthesis. Lysophosphatidic acid is involved in neurodevelopment processes and is highly expressed in the brain.
44
Among the LPA receptors, LPA1 plays a key role in the central nervous system. Previous studies have reported that changes in LPA1 receptors are associated with increased alcohol consumption.
45
Pregnanolone belongs to the neurosteroid family, which influences neuronal function and directly modulates postsynaptic neurotransmitter receptors. Drinking alcohol in adolescence is more likely to develop alcohol dependence in adulthood. Pregnanolone has been shown to be effective in reducing ethanol intake in male rats, and thus, it is a potentially promising agent for alcohol-dependence therapy via positive modulation of GABA
A
receptors.
46
Alcohol may affect some neurotransmitter systems in the brain dysregulating, such as GABA. GABA-benzodiazepine system has an important effect on alcohol fortification behavior.
47
In general, diazepam is useful in the symptomatic management of mild-to-moderate anxiety. Furthermore, there are studies linking diazepam to alcohol consumption. Thirty-day treatment of diazepam has been shown to decrease alcohol consumption relapse
48
; however, another study found that low-dose diazepam increases alcohol intake.
47
In the present study, we found some chemicals related to alcohol dependence, wherein taurine and pesticides have been shown to be involved in the nervous system.
Gene Ontology analysis of significant genes detected several GO terms for alcohol dependence, such as tricarboxylic acid metabolism process, NADP metabolic process, and isocitrate metabolic process. Isocitrate dehydrogenase (NADP (+)) 1 (
IDH1
) and
IDH2
belong to 2 distinct subclasses, one of which uses NAD (+) as the electron acceptor and the other uses NADP (+).
IDH2
acts as a critical part of the TCA by catalyzing the conversion of isocitrate to α-ketoglutarate. Tricarboxylic acid cycle is involved in the synthesis of GABA.
49
The central nucleus of amygdala is an important component of the extended amygdala, and GABAergic transmission in the central nucleus of amygdala is associated with alcohol intake.
50
When offspring of alcohol-dependent humans becomes fearful, the volume of the amygdala and amygdala functional magnetic resonance imaging (fMRI) activation decrease.
51
GABA acts at gamma-aminobutyric acid-A receptors, which are ligand-gated chloride channels. Distinct subunits of gamma-aminobutyric acid-A receptors have been identified, such as γ-aminobutyric acid type A receptor subunit α2 (
GABRA2
). One study found that
GABRA2

Our results provide a new perspective on understanding the complex nature of alcohol dependence pathogenesis. One of highlights in this study is that it used the results of PWAS to identify significant candidate genes for alcohol dependence and explore the relationship between chemicals and alcohol dependence. We first detected genes and chemicals associated with alcohol dependence, and we identified
GOT2
as a promising novel target that warrants further investigation. Nevertheless, some limitations are worth noting. First, all of the subjects in our study were White European thus, the application of our results to other populations should be performed with caution. Second, in our research, the accuracy of our data analysis may be affected by the previous published GWAS. Finally, studies of the biological mechanisms associated with the relationships among identified genes, chemicals, and alcohol dependence are lacking. Larger-scale samples will be required to further confirm our results and elucidate the potential role of this substance in the pathogenesis of alcohol dependence.
CONCLUSIONS
Based on the previous published GWAS data sets, by combining PWAS and functional enrichment analysis, we identified significant genes and chemicals, which may be involved in the development of alcohol dependence. Our study provides novel insights into the impact of genes on alcohol dependence and highlights the importance of chemical effects on substance dependence.
